## What Is a Bates White Internship?


The Summer Consultant Program is Bates White’s flagship 10-week internship, placing participants on real economic consulting engagements at the firm’s sole Washington, DC office. Interns work alongside full-time consultants on active cases spanning antitrust, healthcare, energy, and financial litigation. The program earned the #1 Best Consulting Internship ranking from Vault in 2026, and the firm has been recognized as a WTOP Top DC Workplace for 11 straight years. With structured mentorship, technical training in Stata, Excel, and R, and a clear pathway to full-time Consultant offers, the SCP is one of the most competitive boutique consulting internships in the country.

## What Are the Eligibility Requirements?


Bates White keeps formal requirements minimal but favors candidates with strong quantitative foundations.


• **Education:** Pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree, typically in economics, statistics, mathematics, or a related quantitative field.


• **Quantitative skills:** Proficiency or coursework in Stata, R, or Excel is preferred; experience with econometric modeling is a strong plus.


• **Class year:** Not explicitly stated; rising seniors and penultimate-year master’s students are the typical fit for consulting summer programs.


• **Work authorization:** Not publicly disclosed; contact careers@bateswhite.com to confirm visa sponsorship eligibility.


### Does Bates White Have a GPA Cutoff for Interns?


Bates White does not publish a minimum GPA for the Summer Consultant Program. As the #1 Vault-ranked consulting internship, competition is strong, and peer firms in economic consulting typically see admitted classes with GPAs above 3.5. A standout quantitative transcript, relevant research, or programming experience can offset a slightly lower number.

## What Is the Bates White Application and Interview Process Like?


The Bates White hiring process follows a structured two-round format with behavioral and case components.


1. **Research Bates White’s practice areas.** Review the firm’s expertise in antitrust, healthcare, energy, finance, and IP litigation at bateswhite.com. Understand how economic consulting differs from management consulting.


2. **Prepare your resume.** Highlight quantitative coursework in economics, statistics, or mathematics. Feature programming experience with Stata, R, Excel, or Python and any research or analytical projects.


3. **Submit your application.** Apply through the[Bates White careers portal](https://www.bateswhite.com/careers/current-openings) powered by VI Global Cloud. If you cannot apply digitally, email careers@bateswhite.com.


4. **Attend campus recruiting events (Sep 2–29, 2026).** If Bates White visits your university, attend the information session to make a personal impression and ask questions about the Summer Consultant Program.


5. **Complete the first-round interview (virtual).** Expect behavioral questions and a case interview following Bates White’s three-phase format: brainstorming, calculations, and conceptual discussion.


6. **Complete the second-round interview.** This round (virtual or in-person in DC) includes additional behavioral questions and a second case. Demonstrate structured thinking and comfort connecting quantitative analysis to broader economic concepts.


7. **Receive and evaluate your offer.** Offers typically extend after the second round in late fall. Weigh the program’s #1 Vault ranking, DC location, and strong conversion pipeline.


For interview preparation, review Bates White’s[published example case interview](https://www.bateswhite.com/careers/consultants-and-management/example-case-interview) and[interview tips page](https://www.bateswhite.com/careers/consultants-and-management/interview-tips) .

## How Do You Stand Out at Bates White?


First, study the TalkTek cellphone battery price-fixing case that Bates White publishes on their website. It reveals the firm’s three-phase interview format: brainstorming, calculations, and conceptual discussion. Practice talking through each phase aloud, since the firm values clear reasoning over getting the right answer. Second, build a mini economic analysis project using public data from a recent DOJ antitrust case in Stata or R, then reference it in your application to show genuine interest in economic consulting rather than consulting generically. Third, mention specific firm wins in your interviews, like the unanimous jury verdict against Live Nation/Ticketmaster in a monopolization case, to demonstrate that you understand Bates White’s actual casework.

## FAQ


### What GPA do I need for the Bates White Summer Consultant Program?


Bates White does not publish a minimum GPA requirement. However, as the holder of Vault’s #1 consulting internship ranking, competition is fierce. Peer economic consulting firms typically see admitted interns with GPAs above 3.5. Strong quantitative coursework and relevant analytical experience can help offset a slightly lower GPA.


### How long is the Bates White internship?


The Summer Consultant Program runs for 10 weeks, typically from early June through mid-August. It is a full-time, in-person program based at the firm’s Washington, DC office. The firm uses a hybrid work structure with coordinated in-office days during the program.


### How much does the Bates White internship pay?


The Summer Consultant 2027 role is listed at $37 per hour on Indeed, which translates to roughly $1,480 per week or $14,800 for the full 10-week program. Housing and relocation stipends have not been publicly confirmed. Candidates should verify compensation directly with the firm.


### Does Bates White sponsor visas for interns?


Bates White has not publicly disclosed its visa sponsorship policy for the Summer Consultant Program. The firm does maintain an International Network employee resource group, suggesting a globally diverse workforce. Candidates requiring sponsorship should contact careers@bateswhite.com directly to confirm eligibility before applying.


### What is the Bates White interview process like?


The process consists of two rounds. The first round is virtual and includes behavioral questions plus a case interview. The second round, held virtually or in person at the DC office, adds another behavioral and case component. Cases follow a three-phase format: brainstorming, calculations, and conceptual discussion.


### What is the conversion rate from intern to full-time at Bates White?


Bates White does not disclose a specific intern-to-full-time conversion rate. However, the firm’s career path explicitly positions Summer Consultant as the entry point for full-time Consultant roles, indicating a structured pipeline. Strong performance during the 10-week program positions interns well for return offers.


### What practice areas do Bates White interns work in?


Summer Consultants gain exposure to the firm’s core practice areas, including antitrust and competition, energy, healthcare, finance, intellectual property, and environmental and product liability. Specific case assignments depend on active client engagements and firm needs during the internship. There is no practice-area selection process for interns.


### When should I apply for the Bates White 2027 internship?


Apply now, in August or September 2026. The Summer Consultant 2027 role is already posted, and campus recruiting events run September 2 through 29. Submitting your application before or during the campus recruiting window gives you the strongest chance of securing an interview slot with the firm.
